description: The contract: what the user wants (purpose, requests, examples, promised inputs and outputs, their decisions). How it is done (steps, data, the loop) is the design: comfy_propose_design.

title.description: The workflow's name in the user's words, a few words (e.g. Monthly sales by region): its file name, tab and App title.

purpose.description: 1-3 sentences: who it is for, what it solves, what good looks like.

title.description: A few words naming the request, shown wherever it is referenced (badges, the Design tab): e.g. 'Own cleaning lane per system'.

you_said.description: The user's own words, quoted as said.

we_understood.description: Plain restatement, ideally 'When <situation>, the workflow <does what>.'

examples.description: Concrete input -> expected output pairs that show what the requests mean.

files.description: Small sample files this example runs on: path -> its text (e.g. {"orders/orders.csv": "order_id,region,amount\n1,North,1000\n"}). A file or folder input in given names one of these paths (or its folder, e.g. "orders"); the studio writes them to the input folder for the run. Use them instead of naming files the user has not uploaded.

kind.description: What it holds: a registered kind of the type standard (text, integer, number, boolean, json, table, file: one data file the caller uploads first, folder: a folder of them). Old names resolve (count, csv, …).

description.description: One line a caller reads in the API description: what this input or output holds.

from.description: Outputs: the step output that delivers it ("step.port"); makes it part of the API.

node.description: Inputs: an existing top-level node (e.g. the user's given data folder) that is this input, instead of a new input node.

widget.description: Inputs: the widget on that node the API sets (for a subgraph card, its promoted widget).

by.description: user only for answers the user actually gave.

pattern.description: The design pattern this decision applies, if any.

principle.description: The engineering principle behind it (e.g. single responsibility, determinism).

step.description: The step that waits for the answer; the rest can be built.

open_questions.description: A plain question must be answered before approval. A question tied to one step ({question, step}) may stay open: that step is built around it and cannot be verified until it is answered (by amending the contract).
